source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source C for crop/mung_bean in this knowledge base (Sources A-B were processed in Batch 42).
text: The source gives a nutrient-content comparison table per 100 g for two seed preparations (row labels are only partly legible in the scanned image; the first row is confidently read as "គ្រាប់ដេះ" / dry seed, while the exact wording of the second row label, likely a comparison to sprouted or soaked seed, could not be confirmed and is not guessed here). For the dry-seed row: moisture 10 g, protein 22 g, fat 2 g, carbohydrate 56 g, fiber 0.9 g, iron 3.2 g, and an energy value printed in a form that does not parse as a standard per-100g calorie figure for this crop (see caveat). For the second row: moisture 10 g, protein 22 g, fat 1 g, carbohydrate 60 g, fiber 8 g (unusually high, printed as such), iron 8 g, and a similarly ambiguous energy figure. The table is cited to a "Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000 CLV Network" source.
caveat: Two values in this table are reported as printed rather than corrected: (1) the exact label of the second seed-preparation row could not be confirmed from the scan; (2) the energy/calorie column for both rows reads as a 5-digit Khmer numeral sequence in the source image that does not correspond to a plausible per-100g calorie value for mung bean (typically a few hundred kcal), suggesting either an OCR/scan legibility issue or an unusual number format in the original; the raw digit sequences were not confidently transcribed and are omitted rather than guessed. A future session with a higher-DPI re-scan of this specific table could resolve both points.
